name: Front Raise
description: The front raise is a shoulder isolation exercise targeting the anterior (front) head of the deltoid through shoulder flexion. It can be performed with dumbbells, a barbell, or a plate. It is typically used as an accessory exercise to complement compound overhead pressing movements.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs with palms facing back (pronated) or neutral.
execution.setup_instructions: Use light to moderate weight. The anterior deltoid is frequently overtrained from pressing movements, so this is primarily a finishing or accessory exercise.
steps: With a slight elbow bend, raise both dumbbells in front of you to approximately shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to generate momentum
Raising the dumbbells above shoulder height unnecessarily
safety_considerations: The anterior deltoid is typically already well-trained from pressing movements — program conservatively to avoid overuse
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise to shoulder height. Going higher primarily increases trap involvement.
coaching_cues: Keep your torso still — only your arms should move
Maintain a slight elbow bend throughout — do not lock out
